method_card.title: Quadratic Formula and Completing the Square
method_card.content:
The quadratic formula solves any \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\). The part under the root, \(b^2 - 4ac\), is the discriminant and counts the solutions.

Completing the square rewrites \(x^2 + bx + c\) as \((x + p)^2 + q\) with \(p = \frac{b}{2}\) and \(q = c - p^2\). It solves quadratics and locates the vertex at \((-p, q)\).

steps: Complete the square, then solve: rearrange \((x + p)^2 + q = 0\) to \((x + p)^2 = -q\) and square root both sides for \(x = -p \pm \sqrt{-q}\).
The discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac\) tells you the number of roots: above 0 means two, exactly 0 means one repeated, below 0 means none.
The vertex of \((x + p)^2 + q\) sits at \((-p, q)\), which is how completing the square finds turning points.
